title: Trace slimming and fidelity preservation playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary

This playbook defines a pragmatic, repeatable approach we use to reduce tracing and telemetry volume ("trace slimming") while preserving the fidelity required for SLO debugging, perf regression detection, and billing attribution. It describes policy tiers, schema stability requirements, sampling and compression techniques, and an operational rollout checklist.

Motivation

- Traces and high-cardinality spans are our single largest telemetry cost driver.
- Naive sampling can remove signals critical to post-incident root cause analysis.
- We need a codified process to compress telemetry volume without losing causal chains and attribution for latency/cost SLOs.

Scope

- Applies to server-side request traces, cross-service distributed traces, and high-cardinality runtime span fields produced by Redwood services and runtime components.
- Not in scope: raw user payloads, customer data payloads (PII/PHI), or synthetic telemetry injected for canaries (those have separate retention rules).

Definitions

- Trace slimming: combination of techniques (sampling, field pruning, compression) applied to traces to reduce storage/ingest.
- Fidelity preservation: guarantees and heuristics to keep enough information for post-incident troubleshooting and SLO attribution.
- Anchor spans: minimal set of spans or events retained at full fidelity for each trace to reconstruct causal flow.

Principles

1) Prefer structured, typed fields over free-form strings for all span tags.
2) Classify telemetry by intent: SLO-explain, billing, security-audit, and debugging. Policies differ by intent.
3) Ensure deterministic fallback: if slimming removes fields, reconstructable pointers (IDs/hashes) must remain.
4) Schema compatibility: slimming must not break downstream parsers; use optional/nullable fields and schema version tags.

Policy tiers (recommended defaults)

- Tier A (SLO and billing-critical): keep 100% of spans and full field set for traces that match any of: latency > p99_threshold, error_count > 0, or request flagged as high-cost route. Retain for 90 days.
- Tier B (High-value sampling): retain anchor spans for all traces; sample full-span traces at 5% for low-volume services and 10% for mid-volume; retain for 30 days.
- Tier C (Bulk production): aggressive slimming: keep trace skeleton (root + anchors) + hashed identifiers for 1% full-span retention; drop verbose debug fields. Retain skeletons for 7 days, hashed artifacts for 30 days.

Sampling and slimming algorithms

1) Decision point: classify trace into a tier at the edge (API gateway or runtime ingress) using evaluation order: SLO-conditions -> billing hints -> feature flags -> default sampling.
2) Reservoir sampling for burst resistance: maintain per-service short time-window reservoirs to ensure rare but important traces are kept during spikes.
3) Adaptive scale: increase Tier A upsampling for services with rapid error-rate changes; reduce Tier B sample rate when daily ingest costs exceed budget.

Schema and contract requirements

- Telemetry envelope must include these fields on every trace (names are canonical):
  - trace.id (string)
  - trace.schema_version (string, semver-like)
  - trace.intent (one of: slo,billing,security,debug)
  - trace.tier (A|B|C)
  - service.name (string)
  - span.anchor (boolean) - set on anchor spans
  - cost.hint (optional string) - low|medium|high
  - trace.hashes (list of strings) - stable hashed IDs for reconstructing request associations

- Backwards compatibility: when removing a field, mark it deprecated in schema and keep nil/empty placeholder for two release cycles.

Operational rules and rollout checklist

1) Pre-implementation
   1.1) Create a small synthetic workload that exercises error paths and tail-latency cases for target service.
   1.2) Produce a baseline SLO debug runbook using full-trace capture for 48 hours.
   1.3) Run cost simulation with proposed slimming to estimate ingest delta; target <= 40% reduction without increasing mean time to resolution (MTTR) > 10%.
2) Implementation
   2.1) Implement classification at ingress (edge proxy or runtime coordinator).
   2.2) Emit trace.schema_version and trace.intent on every envelope.
   2.3) Implement anchor selection: prefer root, last-server span, and first-db-call span.
   2.4) Add per-service reservoir sampler with configurable window (defaults: 1m window, reservoir size 200).
3) Canary rollout (2 weeks)
   3.1) Enable Tier B for 5% of traffic for non-critical services; monitor: trace volume, SLI coverage, and MTTR on synthetic incidents.
   3.2) If false negatives in debugging increase by > 5% on canary, revert and increase anchor retention.
4) Full rollout
   4.1) Ramp sampling rates per success gates: cost delta within target AND no MTTR regression.
   4.2) Document new runbooks and update on-call playbooks to reference trace anchors and trace.hashes for lookups.

Monitoring and SLOs for the playbook

- Trace coverage SLI: fraction of incidents (postmortems) where traces collected had sufficient anchors to produce a flame graph >= 95% (target). Measurement via manual labeling and periodic audits.
- Ingest cost SLO: daily telemetry ingest cost must not exceed budgeted target for the service (defined per-team).
- MTTR regression guardrail: change must not increase median incident MTTR for severity 2 events by more than 10%.

Alerting thresholds

- If daily trace volume reduction target missed by > 20% after rollout, page telemetry-owner.
- If the number of incidents lacking reconstructable anchors in a 7-day window exceeds 3, trigger rollback.
Implementation examples

- Example anchor span selection policy (pseudocode):

  for trace in incoming_traces:
    if trace.latency > p99_threshold or trace.error_count > 0:
      set trace.tier = "A"
      mark root_span.anchor = true
      mark last_server_span.anchor = true
    else:
      set trace.tier = classify_by_cost_hint(trace) or "C"
      mark spans per policy: root + heuristics

- Skeleton payload example (JSON-like, for downstream ingestion):

  {
    "trace.id": "abc123",
    "trace.schema_version": "1.4.0",
    "trace.intent": "slo",
    "trace.tier": "B",
    "service.name": "runtime-inference-proxy",
    "spans": [
      {"id": "s1", "anchor": true, "name": "proxy.receive", "start_ms": 1650000000},
      {"id": "s4", "anchor": false, "name": "model.invoke", "start_ms": 1650000030, "trace.hashes": ["h1"]}
    ]
  }

Compatibility with downstream systems

- Downstream parsers must treat unknown optional fields as ignorable.
- Ingest pipelines should map trace.schema_version to parsing code path to avoid runtime errors.

Ownership and governance

- Observability Platform owns the playbook and core reservoir sampler library.
- Service teams own per-service policy config and are responsible for validating their SLO coverage during canary rollouts.
- Quarterly audit: Observability Platform runs an audit sampling 100 postmortems to validate anchor coverage and issues a remediation list.

Appendix A — Configuration table (recommended defaults)

- reservoir.window = "1m"
- reservoir.size = "200"
- tierB.sample_rate = "0.05"
- tierB.full_capture_rate = "0.10"
- tierC.skeleton_retention_days = "7"
- tierA.full_retention_days = "90"

Appendix B — CLI snippets and example rollout commands

- Enable Tier B for service: 
  ./telemetryctl set-sampling --service runtime-inference-proxy --tier B --sample-rate 0.05 --window 60s

- Inspect anchor coverage (example query):
  SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE span.anchor = true) / count(*) FROM traces WHERE service.name = 'runtime-inference-proxy' AND timestamp > now() - interval '7 days';

Appendix C — Frequently asked questions

Q: Will slimming make debugging impossible for third-party integrators?
A: No — Tier A retains full traces for error and high-latency paths. For partner debugging we provide on-demand full-capture windows and a short-term elevated retention API.

Q: How do we handle PII?
A: Do not include PII in span fields. If a customer request requires more detailed payloads for debugging, use the secured one-time export flow and mark traces as confidentiality = restricted.

Related work and references

- Telemetry ingestion and retention guidelines (see related_pages).
- Reservoir sampling paper references and adaptive sampling literature.

Contact
